solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: First couple of thuds below make an alarming sound (7)

indicatorNotes.First couple of: a couple is two, so take the first two letters of the word that follows

blocks.note: the opening two letters of THUDS

annotation.surface: Someone hears a pair of thuds from downstairs and takes fright.
annotation.walkthrough: The definition is a verb phrase, so 'make' belongs to it rather than acting as a link.
annotation.definitionFit: Used as a verb, it describes a loud menacing rumble, like a storm overhead, which alarms.

indicatorNotes.mistreated: letters that are mistreated are knocked about and end up out of order

annotation.surface: A student who stirs things up confesses to having treated someone badly.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Controversial student' reads as one phrase, but the definition stops after the first word and the student is only fodder.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a tendentious argument pushes one side of a disputed question, so it provokes controversy.

entries.clue: Out of bed, stiff and tense (7)

blocks.note: up = out of bed, as in 'already up'
tight = stiff, as a lid or joint that won't move

annotation.surface: Someone gets out of bed aching and stiff.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is about morning stiffness; 'tense' is the only word describing a state of mind.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym from informal speech: someone wound up with nerves is described with either word.

entries.clue: Be rude to a contemporary in speech — and scarper! (9)

indicatorNotes.in speech: something rendered in speech is heard rather than read, so go by its sound

blocks.note: to dis (diss) someone is to insult them
a peer is someone of your own age or standing

annotation.surface: Advice to insult someone your own age and then run for it.
annotation.walkthrough: Scarper is British slang for running away, and the dash and exclamation mark turn it into a command.
annotation.definitionFit: Scarper is British slang for bolting from a scene, which leaves you gone from sight.

entries.clue: Instructions of great length queen overturned (6)

indicatorNotes.overturned: in a down clue, something turned over is upside down, so it reads from the bottom up

blocks.note: an epic film or poem is a very long one

annotation.surface: A long list of commands that brought a queen down.
annotation.walkthrough: Both pieces are turned over together, not just the queen.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym by example: a cook follows a set of step-by-step directions for a dish.

indicatorNotes.lying about: something lying about has been turned about, so it faces the other way

annotation.surface: Friends are telling lies about a punch-up.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Lying' pretends to mean telling fibs; with 'about' it tells the solver to lay the friends the other way round.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a smack with the open hand is one kind of blow.

indicatorNotes.reported: what is reported is passed on by word of mouth, so go by sound

annotation.surface: Only a handful of problems were reported.
annotation.walkthrough: The definition is the schoolroom sense of problem, an arithmetic exercise.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: a calculation set at school is a maths problem.

entries.clue: Come to American and Irish funeral festivities (5)

blocks.note: the gathering, often lively, held around a death in Ireland

annotation.surface: An invitation to an American and Irish send-off for the dead.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Come to' looks like an invitation to attend the funeral, but it means regain consciousness.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom: to come to after fainting is to become conscious again.

indicatorNotes.backing: going backwards, so read the school name in reverse

blocks.note: the famous English boarding school; in Britain 'public school' means an elite fee-paying one

annotation.surface: A public school supports a boy's comments in a report.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Backing' reads as supporting, but it reverses the school; the son's letter goes after.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: brief written comments, as in a margin, are remarks.

indicatorNotes.to drop back: the word is told to drop its back, meaning its last letter

annotation.surface: An officer orders a soldier to fall back.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Drop back' sounds like a retreat on the battlefield; here the soldier's back end is what drops.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: an officer's order to troops is exactly that, and the noun and verb senses both match.

indicatorNotes.off: the letters are off, gone bad or out of place

annotation.surface: A dispirited soldier deserted.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Made off' reads as fled; 'made' is fodder and 'off' alone is the indicator.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both describe someone whose morale and confidence have drained away.

blocks.note: the surface wants a meal eaten by someone; the setter means the state a bird starts from
not the proverbial early riser but a bird at its earliest, not yet hatched

annotation.surface: What the proverbial early riser eats first thing.
annotation.walkthrough: The early bird of the proverb is an early riser, but read literally a bird is at its earliest before hatching, and the answer is also a breakfast staple.
annotation.definitionFit: It is both a common breakfast food and the first stage of any bird's life.

indicatorNotes.Somehow: arranged in some way or other, so rearrange

annotation.surface: Someone manages to admire Pep Guardiola, the football manager, which seems unlikely to last.
annotation.walkthrough: The 's of Pep's is just surface glue; only its letters PEP go into the mix.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom, supposedly from opium smoking: a hope as unreal as a drug-induced vision.

entries.clue: Beside themselves, as TV housewives were (9)

blocks.note: the adjective in the title of the American TV drama about suburban wives

annotation.surface: Television housewives lose control of themselves.
annotation.walkthrough: The second half refers to Desperate Housewives, the American TV drama.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom and a title: being beside yourself is being frantic, and the TV wives were named for that state.

entries.clue: Giggle time after time in bank (6)

indicatorNotes.after: one T is placed after the other
indicatorNotes.in: the pair go inside the bank

blocks.note: a tier is a bank, a rising row as of seats

annotation.surface: Someone keeps giggling at the bank counter.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Bank' is a row of seats rising one above another, not the money kind.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a nervous, half-suppressed giggle.

indicatorNotes.in: one word goes inside the other

blocks.note: Ur, the Sumerian city in the Bible, is the crossword's favourite ancient city
sure = safe, as in 'a safe bet'

annotation.surface: A moneylender keeps a strongbox in an old city.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Safe' pretends to be a strongbox; it is the adjective.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym with a sting: the word is used of a lender charging extortionate interest.

entries.clue: Managed to get rid of loot (7)

blocks.note: to sack is to get rid of, dismiss

annotation.surface: Someone succeeded in disposing of stolen goods.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Loot' reads as a noun, the stolen goods; it is the verb, to plunder.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to go through a place grabbing valuables is to plunder it.

entries.clue: Lexicon or dictionary featuring this type of language? (6)

indicatorNotes.featuring: the answer is featured inside the words

blocks.note: starts at the last letter of the first word and runs into the start of the third

annotation.surface: A question about which language a word list covers.
annotation.walkthrough: The run is lexico(N OR DIC)tionary; 'this type of language' points back at the hiding place.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by class: the Scandinavian tongues such as Norwegian and Swedish go by this name.

indicatorNotes.thumped: the letters are beaten out of shape

annotation.surface: An American rugby prop hit an opponent intentionally.
annotation.walkthrough: A prop is a rugby forward, which is why thumping someone deliberately fits the surface.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: an adverbial phrase meaning with intent, not by accident.

indicatorNotes.might one say: what one might say is spoken aloud, so go by sound

annotation.surface: Someone wonders whether a little bit of quiet is on offer.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Bit quiet' reads as 'rather quiet'; split it into the definition and the sound-alike.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a portion or fragment of something.

indicatorNotes.endlessly: without an end, so the word loses its final letter
indicatorNotes.about: turned about, so what is left faces the other way

blocks.note: a row, as of people or type

annotation.surface: A quarrel that goes on and on over nothing.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Row' tempts as a quarrel, which 'endlessly' seems to extend; here it is a line.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym from sport: a score of zero, especially in football.

indicatorNotes.back: pulled back means drawn backwards, so the word reads in reverse
indicatorNotes.holding: the reversed word holds the note inside

blocks.note: te, the seventh note of the sol-fa scale

annotation.surface: A flight attendant draws back while holding a message.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Note' pretends to be a message; it is a musical note.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: the person who looks after passengers on a ship or plane.

entries.clue: Two articles about heroin, I see (3)

indicatorNotes.about: the two articles go around the heroin

blocks.note: a and a, two indefinite articles

annotation.surface: Someone spots two newspaper pieces about heroin.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Articles' suggest newspaper stories; they are the grammatical article, twice.
annotation.definitionFit: Both are exclamations of sudden understanding, so one swaps for the other in speech.

blocks.note: a = for each, as in '£5 a head'
Mass is the Catholic church service

annotation.surface: A call to congregate for every church service.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Gather' sounds like assembling for worship; it is the definition, meaning collect.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to pile up or accumulate a quantity of something.

entries.clue: Bishop had to return second class (4)

indicatorNotes.to return: going back, so read the word in reverse

blocks.note: B = bishop, as in chess notation

annotation.surface: A bishop was obliged to go back and travel second class.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Had to' reads as 'was obliged to'; the two words split between the piece and its reversal.
annotation.definitionFit: The second Greek letter is used as a grade for second-class work.

entries.clue: Inspected, as one’s bags may be? (7)

blocks.note: luggage handed over at the airport desk to travel in the hold

annotation.surface: Luggage going through an airport search.
annotation.walkthrough: At an airport, bags are both inspected and checked in, handed over for the hold.
annotation.definitionFit: Two senses: looked over for faults, and luggage checked in to travel in the hold.
